This plan covers the work that follows the 16.0.0 modernization:

  • storage behind one write path;
  • the client and server identifiers Loop asked to separate;
  • controller registration, from a read-only catalogue to typed writes;
  • multitenant Nightscout.

It names each piece of work, what it needs first, where it goes in the code, and the check that pins it.

1. 16.0.0 scope (maintainer, 2026-10-30)

16.0.0 targets every single-tenant item of this plan, through the entry bar and in priority order. A miss rolls to 16.1.0, or to 17.0.0 if it changes a default. - The identity work is the core. It is the substance of the agreement with the Loop maintainers: identifier-first on every path, re-sends recognised, the format rules, and one record per identifier. - The unique index on identifier is in 16.0.0, behind WRITE_IDENTIFIER_INDEX=try|require|off (default try). - Under try, boot attempts a partial unique index per collection: records with an identifier, soft-deleted ones included, built online. If existing duplicates block it, the counts per collection (never the values) are logged and shown on the status page, and the server runs without the index. - The write rule (ID-Q5) still refuses to create a second record with a stored identifier. - require refuses to start until the index exists. off skips it. - An operator-run tool reports duplicate groups and resolves them by the P4 pick. - Multitenant items may ship dormant, labelled alpha behind serve, or not ship.

Feasibility, from the 7 days to 2026-10-30: 53 PRs merged into dev, and 14 of this plan's 36 items went to done. Build speed is not the limit. Time on dev, cohort checks and review are, so items land in priority order and early, and the tag is gated by the bar, not by a date.

2. Why the tracks meet at the write step

Every track changes what happens when a record is written:

track what it needs from the write step
Identity a single place that matches a re-sent record on identifier first, then on the time key, for v1, v3 and the socket alike
Registration a single place that applies a controller's declared schema to its typed writes, and leaves unregistered writers byte-identical
Validation a single place for #8841's rules, so the socket and the v1 modules are not checked separately
Tenancy a single place that carries the tenant binding, so no path can write without one

8854 built that place as a boundary at the driver call, and the storage interface sits above it. Each later slice adds one rule there. Every slice must keep the following:

must hold pinned by
the _id forms: ObjectId, upper- and lower-case hex, UUID, and UUID_HANDLING moving a non-hex _id to identifier #8854's matrix rows; tests/identity-matrix.test.js
the API v3 create and deduplication reply (status, identifier, isDeduplication, lastModified), and AndroidAPS's string-matched refusal texts tests/write-validation.test.js; the v3 suites
Loop's syncIdentifier and Trio's id stored and returned untouched write-contract matrix
v1 treatment upsert on created_at + eventType write-contract matrix

The forward constraints are two mature backends behind one interface (D2–D4), the closed query operator set as a filter tree (D8), a source label and later a tenant binding on every write, and one commit fact the change feed can carry (D6; D-EVENT deferred, with its reopen conditions on its card in §5). Under #8854's merge conditions, the commit event stays internal and unstable, and the intent layer gets its own name.

item builds needs check

Rules in force (maintainer, 2026-10-26 and 2026-10-27):

  • Null removes. An explicit null removes a field on merge-on-match, API v3 PATCH and the socket's dbUpdate (RFC 7386; write contract §6.1). It never does so on PUT or create, and devicestatus never merges.
  • Fallback. A v1 entries re-send whose identifier matches nothing still matches on sysTime+type; treatments never fall back. A devicestatus re-send whose identifier is stored merges by default since ID-Q2 (2026-10-29); WRITE_RESEND=acknowledge keeps the earlier rule (write nothing, answer with the stored _id).
  • Absent identifier. identifier is SHOULD for legacy writers, and the time-key fallback stays. It is MUST for registered controller instances. Revisited as adoption grows.
  • Scope. Uniqueness is per collection, with the tenant in the key under multi. Values stay globally unique by convention.
  • Re-send after delete. It is acknowledged with a 2xx naming the stored, deleted record, and the record stays deleted.
  • Format (2026-10-29, D-LOOP-ID rule 1 and ID-Q6). Any string of 1 to 256 characters, with no character restriction, percent-encoded in a URL path; a UUID is recommended. A placeholder or over-length value is treated as absent with a warning; refusing it is WRITE_IDENTIFIER=strict, off by default. Which placeholders are named is open (ID-PLACEHOLDER-LIST, identity specification §5).
  • _id (2026-10-29). A client may still send an ObjectId _id over API v1 (legacy). Going forward the server sets _id and the client sets identifier.
  • Merge on match (2026-10-29). When a re-send matching a stored record is applied, fields it leaves out are kept (RFC 7386), and PUT replaces. The census reads replace on several paths today. The extended matrix measures each path first, and each path that changes is listed cell by cell.
  • Re-send after delete, every path (2026-10-29). "Acknowledged, stays deleted" applies on every path, and the spec text is corrected. Every changed cell is documented, so the change can be reverted or adjusted as cohort feedback arrives.
  • Records without an identifier. Natural keys for device status and profile are a separate item, ID-NATURAL-KEY, with its own corpus check of what would merge. Food and activity have no natural key.
  • Socket edits and removes, and activity. Identifier addressing is added where it changes nothing for writes that carry no identifier: socket dbUpdate, dbUpdateUnset and dbRemove accept an identifier when there is no _id, and activity creates match on identifier. This is conditional on the extended matrix showing every existing form unchanged.
  • Re-send with changed fields (2026-10-29). Merge on match stays the default, because Loop and Trio re-send changed doses, overrides and temp targets by POST (client survey). API v3 keeps refusing a changed date, device or event type, and PUT replaces. A site setting plus per-client quirks (D20) may opt a client into keep-first or refuse. A default changes only in a major: 16.0.0 if it clears the entry bar (§1a), otherwise 17.0.0.

The rules are in the identity specification and the identifier conventions; the conversation with the Loop maintainers is in upstream-asks-loop-identifier.

D-EVENT: Commit event (deferred)

maintainer; deferred 2026-10-27, research continuing · holds up ST-EVENT

No shape is adopted for storage-write-committed; it stays counts-only and internal. Prototyping and measuring continue as input. Reopen when all four are in hand: (1) WC-STEP-PATCH's WriteResult.items[], so records are named from the write's own result, as API v3's storage events already are; (2) a named first subscriber and its exactness need (screen refresh, or sync and alarms); (3) the BF-164 AndroidAPS websocket cursor finding re-measured; (4) a count of sites running on a replica set, where change streams are the exact source.

  1. Reopen with the four inputsrecommendedGains: the shape is chosen against a real subscriber and the write's own resultRisks: none until something subscribes
  2. Read before the write, capped (500 measured)Gains: about x1.00 on large backfills, exact below the cap; the shape Nocturne usesRisks: writes over the cap give an event with no records, so a listener re-reads
  3. Read records after the writeGains: free on fresh backfillsRisks: a full re-send costs about what the pre-read does; misses updates that move records out of their filter (0 of 5 exact); inexact 2-4 times as often under the pruner race; no surveyed system does this

D-LOOP-ID: identity rules decided 2026-10-29; Loop's answers awaited

maintainer (the reply's channel; the three rules after the Loop maintainers answer) · holds up nothing yet

The revised reply to the Loop maintainers was posted on the project site on 2026-10-27; their answers are awaited. The maintainer decided 2026-10-29 to proceed without waiting, revisable when Loop answers: (1) identifier format: 1 to 256 URL-safe characters, a UUID recommended, placeholders (invalid, undefined, null, NaN) refused; (2) _id: a client may still send an ObjectId _id over API v1 (legacy); going forward the server sets _id and the client sets identifier. (3) decided the same day after a client survey: merge on match stays the default (Loop's doses and early-ended overrides and Trio's finalized doses and temp targets are re-sent by POST over v1 and rely on the update; a refusal makes them retry silently without end); API v3 keeps refusing a changed date, device or event type; PUT replaces; a site setting plus per-client D20 quirks may select keep-first or refuse for clients that opt in, and a default changes only in a major (16.0.0 if it clears the entry bar, otherwise 17.0.0). The published reply's case 2 is corrected and Loop's dropped carb edits (an _id cached for 24 h) raised. (Absent identifier, scope and re-send after delete were decided earlier, §4.2.)

6. How the work moves

  • Pull requests. Sized by milestone, not by slice: the single-tenant registration PR (S0, S1, S2, S5); storage slices grouped into few PRs. A track with many pieces in flight uses an integration branch with child PRs, the way #8605 carried 109 children. Dev is merged into a branch, not rebased, and a PR's merge records that the merged tree matches the reviewed tree.
  • What pins behaviour. #8854's CRUD matrix and this repository's write-contract matrix (tools/qc/write-contract-matrix.js; v1, v3, socket and in-process). A slice that changes no behaviour changes no cell; a slice that changes behaviour lists the cells it changes and why.
  • Red controls. Every new test is shown failing against the code it guards before the change, with the original symptom.
  • Conformance. The registration and identity cases in specs/sync/conformance/ run against a booted server by a harness in this repository (D12), reported case by case as passed, mapped or not applicable.
  • Agents. Agents build slices in their own worktrees, run the checks and hand back a branch, a PR body and the push commands. They never push. Maintainers push, open, review and merge.
  • Releases. #8865 (one executable, the image's start and stop, the boot split; serve reserved for a multitenant Nightscout, every role refused until it is multitenant) merged into 16.0.0 on 2026-10-30. Since 2026-10-30 every single-tenant item of this plan targets 16.0.0 through the entry bar (§1); a miss merges after the tag, one theme per minor; the 16.0.0 quiet period starts when its merge list is closed, not on a date. Components shipped before they are mature are labelled alpha; the label belongs to the multitenant bindings, not to code every single-tenant site runs.
  • Records. Each landed slice updates its queue item (queue/work-queue.yaml) and this plan's data file, and the page is re-rendered.
